summary: Today’s pulse tracks Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises, Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer, and Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are attack, senate, and sunday. In the background, Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker and Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over media freedom keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises
headlines.description: Mississippi Democrat points to commitments Trump made: lower prices, halt endless wars and release Epstein files After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024. Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.

headlines.title: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer
headlines.description: Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer , asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances. Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.

headlines.title: Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs
headlines.description: Total of 75 have already signed letter to Burnham opposing plans as discontent also grows over Europe and welfare changes As many as 100 Labour MPs could sign a letter opposing the giant Rosebank oilfield, as discontent among backbenchers looks likely to surge this week, with rebellions also brewing over Europe and welfare changes. A total of 75 MPs have already signed the private letter, which is expected to be delivered in the next fortnight to Andy Burnham as part of a campaign in which Labour MPs from the party’s 2024 intake are playing a significant role.

headlines.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
headlines.description: Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone maker in the Baltic state over the weekend, which authorities said was ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service. On Saturday morning, eight people were detained during an attempted attack on Threod Systems, a defence company that manufactures long-range attack and reconnaissance drones. No injuries or damage were reported after the company’s security team responded to the incident.

headlines.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over media freedom
headlines.description: Estimated 350,000 people rally against plan to scrap licence fees and fund broadcasters from state budget Hundreds of thousands of Czechs have rallied in Prague to protest against a perceived government attempt to stifle media freedom. The gathering on Sunday to save the mandatory licence fees that fund Czechia’s public broadcasters drew more than 350,000 people, making it one of the biggest in the country’s history, organisers said.

headlines.title: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
headlines.description: The Ukrainian president says restrictions are still in place and making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.

headlinePool.title: Iran launches drone attacks against US military base in Bahrain
headlinePool.description: Strikes cast further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington with increasing risk of escalation Iran has launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain, casting further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington and raising the spectre of escalation. Blasts sounded over the Gulf nation on Sunday in the second Iranian drone attack in three days in retaliation for US strikes in Iran.

headlinePool.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
headlinePool.description: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.

headlinePool.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
headlinePool.description: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.

headlinePool.title: Burnham pledges early intervention and ‘benefits backstop’ to tackle youth jobs crisis
headlinePool.description: Prime minister promises ‘root-and-branch rethink’ of support for young people as Milburn report advises sweeping changes to some benefits Andy Burnham: The crisis facing Britain’s young people is politicians’ fault. To fix it, we need a generational response Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”. Burnham said the government would intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fell behind, and “long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state”, including providing more opportunities for vocational training in schools.

headlinePool.title: Planned asylum seeker detention centre next to Oxfordshire sewage works criticised
headlinePool.description: Thames Water says detainees at proposed accommodation should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells A Home Office plan to build asylum seeker detention facilities next to a sewage pump is facing objections after water company officials warned that detainees should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells. Proposed secure accommodation blocks at Campsfield House immigration removal centre in Oxfordshire will be 20 metres from a sewage pumping station, according to a written submission from Thames Water.

headlinePool.title: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage
headlinePool.description: Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades. “I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop , leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights.

headlinePool.title: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain - as it happened
headlinePool.description: Iran has targeted airbase in Bahrain in latest resumption of strikes since september The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning. Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain. The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples. The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace. This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression. The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region , disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.

headlinePool.title: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
headlinePool.description: The temporary order is part of a months-long challenge to the US president's plans to upgrade East Potomac Golf Links into a championship course.

headlinePool.title: Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding
headlinePool.description: Two people injured after wingtip of Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck nose of United Parcel Service Boeing 767 Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international airport on Saturday night – a day after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an hours-long nationwide ground stop due to communication issues affecting multiple air traffic control centers. In a statement, the Trump administration-led FAA said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service Boeing 767 “while the airplanes were taxiing at Miami International Airport”.
